headline: AI Platform Helps WFP Reach Hungry Somalis Before Crisis Hits
meta_description: Somalia's World Food Programme uses artificial intelligence to predict hunger crises and deliver aid faster to vulnerable communities.
summary_short: AI tools are helping the UN's World Food Programme identify hungry communities in Somalia before conditions worsen, enabling faster, smarter aid delivery.
body:
Artificial intelligence is transforming how aid workers respond to hunger in Somalia, allowing them to reach families before malnutrition becomes irreversible. The UN's World Food Programme uses HungerMap Live, an AI-powered platform that analyses data on rainfall, food prices, conflict, and nutrition to forecast where hunger will strike next. In Burhakaba District, northwest of Mogadishu, WFP workers identified dangerously malnourished children using these AI tools and mobilised food assistance for 48,000 people and nutrition support for 3,000 women and children. "Instead of waiting for that malnutrition of children to deteriorate and lead to displacement or even death, we knew it prior," said Simon Renk, WFP's head of vulnerability analysis in Somalia.

Somalia faces a perfect storm of hunger: a 35-year conflict, climate-driven droughts and floods, and dependence on imported food that exposes the country to global price shocks. With 6 million Somalis facing crisis-level food insecurity, WFP can only reach one in ten people in need. The newly upgraded HungerMap Live 2.0, released in April, does more than identify current hunger—it predicts where conditions will worsen next, helping governments and aid agencies prioritise resources with stronger evidence.

Yet AI alone cannot solve the scale of the crisis. "This platform helps us to prioritise with stronger evidence," Renk acknowledged, "but in itself, it doesn't make the shortage of support acceptable." WFP needs an additional $192 million through January 2027 to reach everyone who needs help. Still, by shortening the time between early warning and action, AI is proving that smarter tools can save lives when resources are scarce.
quick_facts: HungerMap Live 2.0 uses AI to predict hunger crises across 90+ countries
In Burhakaba District, WFP reached 48,000 people with food aid using AI insights
6 million Somalis face crisis food insecurity; WFP can reach only 1 in 10
$192 million needed by January 2027 to reach all those in need
